document.summary: The saved baseline ranking places usability and quality issues first by priority score, driven by the largest complaint volume in this self-selected historical review sample, with billing concerns second and the coarse other-complaints bucket third. Playback interruptions rank lower in volume but show the highest mean severity among the larger topics, and the bounded examples include expressed cancellation intent, which is distinct from observed churn; no actual churn outcome is established by this dataset. The recommended next-quarter priority is the usability and quality topic, with a focus on the subtopics visible in the bounded examples: app crashes after updates, difficulty accessing saved playlists, and sound quality complaints. Billing subscription-state confusion is the strongest alternative given its higher mean severity than usability. All proposed benefits are hypotheses to be tested; the sample is self-selected app-store feedback and cannot establish prevalence, revenue at risk, or causal retention effects.
limitations: The dataset is a self-selected sample of app-store reviews and cannot establish population prevalence, revenue at risk, or causal retention improvement from any proposed fix.
Expressed cancellation intent appears in some bounded examples but is distinct from observed churn; no churn outcomes are present in the supplied data.
A portion of reviews were flagged as needing review and their labels are uncertain; the saved ranking may shift once those labels are resolved.
Topic grouping is coarse; the other-complaints bucket aggregates heterogeneous negative feedback, and a topic's aggregate count does not establish the prevalence of any particular subtopic within it.
Severity is a model-assigned label under a shared rubric, not a score reported by reviewers, and human benchmark accuracy for the labeling is unestablished in the supplied data.
The bounded examples cover only a subset of reviews per topic; subtopic conclusions such as crash-after-update or playlist-display failures are supported only by the quoted examples shown.
Proposed product benefits are hypotheses to be validated through controlled evaluation, not measured causal effects.

alternatives.title: Billing subscription-state fixes as the primary priority
alternatives.rationale: This alternative is attractive because its mean severity exceeds that of the top-ranked topic, and the bounded examples include paying users blocked from their music. It was not chosen as primary because its complaint volume is lower than the top topic in this self-selected sample, and the examples mix subscription-state confusion with feature-gating complaints that may need different owners.

alternatives.title: Playback reliability as the primary priority
alternatives.rationale: Playback interruptions show the highest mean severity among the larger topics in the saved claims, and the bounded examples include random stops on tablets with explicit cancellation intent and forced-shuffle frustration. It was not chosen as primary because its complaint volume is materially lower than the top topic in this sample, and the examples span distinct subtopics such as shuffle restrictions and mobile-data failures that may not share a single fix.

alternatives.title: Offline download reliability as the primary priority
alternatives.rationale: Download failures have a small volume in this sample but the bounded examples include a paying subscriber whose downloaded content disappears and who states intent to move elsewhere, which is expressed cancellation intent rather than observed churn. It was not chosen as primary because the sample volume is the smallest among actionable topics, limiting confidence that the subtopic generalizes.

recommendations.title: Prioritize post-update stability and playlist access fixes
recommendations.rationale: This topic holds the top rank in the saved baseline by priority score and complaint volume, and the bounded examples describe crashes following a new interface, playlists not displaying saved music, and sound quality complaints. Some examples express cancellation intent, which is not the same as observed churn. A focused fix-and-validate effort on these subtopics is the highest-ranked actionable area; expected retention benefit is a hypothesis to test, not a measured effect.

recommendations.title: Instrument and triage subscription-state confusion signals
recommendations.rationale: Billing ranks second by priority score and shows a higher mean severity than the top-ranked topic in the saved claims. The bounded examples describe paying subscribers seeing upgrade prompts and pause-subscription screens despite active premium status. Because these examples touch paying users, a diagnostic instrumentation effort is warranted as a companion action, with any retention benefit treated as untested.
